evals.name: confluence-prd-plus-jira-tickets
evals.prompt: Structure a Confluence page for a PRD (CSV export feature, 5-50 seat B2B admins, 3-page PRD ready), and open the corresponding Jira tickets: one epic + the MVP-slice stories. Produce the Confluence page (title, metadata block, TL;DR, sections) AND the Jira ticket templates (epic + 4 stories with acceptance criteria + links + labels). Don't re-invent the PRD content — just structure and link.
evals.expected_output: A Confluence page skeleton with title convention, status block, owner, TL;DR placement, section headings matching the PRD template; AND 5 Jira tickets (1 epic + 4 stories) each with title, user value, acceptance criteria, scope IN/OUT, links bidirectional (PRD ↔ epic ↔ stories), labels, DoD. Structure > content.

evals.name: ticket-hygiene-pass
evals.prompt:
Hygiene pass on these 4 badly-written tickets. Refactor each to our standard. Tickets:

1. 'add csv' — description: 'user wants csv'. Status: in backlog 3 months.
2. 'Fix the thing with the export' — description: 'broken since last week, user reported on slack'. No steps to reproduce.
3. 'Build backend API for export' — description: 'POST /export, returns CSV, uses job queue'. No user story, no acceptance criteria.
4. 'Epic: improve onboarding' — 23 child stories, no primary metric, no bet statement, no MVP/R2 slicing.

Produce a refactored version of each with title, body, acceptance criteria, links, labels, and note any questions you'd ask the PM before promoting to Ready.
evals.expected_output: 4 refactored tickets each with: proper title (imperative, user-outcome for stories; symptom for bugs; specific for chores), description following the right template (story vs bug vs epic vs task), acceptance criteria, scope, links, labels, DoD. Plus open questions needed before Ready.
